citation: Jaciw, A. P., Schellinger, A. M., Lin, L., Zacamy, J., & Toby, M. (2016). Effectiveness of Internet-Based Reading Apprenticeship Improving Science Education (iRAISE): A Report of a Randomized Experiment in Michigan and Pennsylvania (Empirical Education Rep. No. Empirical_iRAISE-7027-FR1-Y2-O.3). Palo Alto, CA: Empirical Education Inc.
report_number: Empirical Education Rep. No. Empirical_iRAISE-7027-FR1-Y2-O.3; i3 Development grant U411C120094 to WestEd
design: Cluster (teacher-level) randomized controlled trial. 82 high-school science teachers in 47 schools across Michigan and Pennsylvania were randomly assigned within matched pairs to iRAISE professional development (41 teachers) vs business-as-usual control (41 teachers); intent-to-treat. Intervention = iRAISE = Internet-based Reading Apprenticeship Improving Science Education, an online adaptation of WestEd Strategic Literacy Institute's 65-hour biology-based Reading Apprenticeship literacy PD (5-day summer Foundations + monthly Ignite/PLC follow-ups Sept-May), delivered to grade 9-12 science teachers during the 2014-15 school year. Comparison = business-as-usual. Outcome subject = general reading/disciplinary literacy (assessed in science classrooms); grades 9-12. Analytic student sample with ETS posttests = 1,468 students (717 iRAISE / 751 control) taught by 69 teachers (35 iRAISE / 34 control) in 46 schools (23 / 23), 31-34 assignment pairs. Impacts estimated via multilevel/HLM models (SAS PROC MIXED/GLIMMIX; students nested in teachers nested in matched pairs/schools) adjusting for pretest and covariates.
problems: IDENTIFICATION NUANCE: The meta-analysis label 'Jaciw, Hegseth et al. 2016' does not exactly match this report's author list (Jaciw, Schellinger, Lin, Zacamy, Toby). Whitney Hegseth is NOT an author of the iRAISE impact report; she co-authored the sibling RAISE scale-up report (Newman, Zacamy, Lazarev, Lin, Jaciw, Hegseth, 2015) and is in the RAISE impact report acknowledgements. Despite the imperfect author string, iRAISE is the correct report for registry row 50: it uniquely matches every registry attribute -- Andrew Jaciw lead author, 2016, Teacher/Class-level cluster RCT, grades 7-12 (9-12), Average/High SES, 'Comprehensive approaches' TPD goal (Reading Apprenticeship is a comprehensive disciplinary-literacy instructional framework), 'Short' duration (1-year online PD), Res/Dev test (the ETS scenario-based literacy assessment), and 'Three' principles (performance standards + self-regulation + cooperation, coaching=0). The separate RAISE *impact* report (Fancsali et al. 2015, ERIC ED571000, same ETS literacy outcome) is already extracted as a DISTINCT study at registry row 29 (coded School/QED/(P)CK/Long/Two-principles), so iRAISE (row 50) is genuinely a different study, not a duplicate. The RAISE *scale-up* report -- the only RAISE document with Hegseth as author -- explicitly 'didn't consider student achievement as a variable' (its Chapter 8 only does exploratory teacher-level value-added correlations drawn from the Fancsali RCT), so it yields no extractable TPD-vs-control student achievement g; iRAISE is the only report attributable to row 50 that contains a genuine TPD-vs-control student achievement contrast. VARIANCE NUANCE: the report gives effect sizes and p-values but does not report a clean SE on the same standardized metric as the headline ES. The headline adjusted ES (0.002) is standardized by the pooled posttest SD of the recalibrated ETS scale (0.2456; reproduced: adjusted mean difference .0005 / 0.2456 = 0.00204). The model coefficient SEs in Tables 17-18 are on a within-grade z-transformed outcome (different scale), so I did not transplant the .004 coefficient SE onto the 0.002 ES. Instead g_se/g_var are derived from the report's own stated precision: MDES = 0.19 SD at alpha=.05, 80% power (p.5), giving SE = 0.19/2.80 = 0.068, g_var = 0.0046; this design-based SE properly reflects the teacher-level clustering (cluster_adjusted=true). No empirical ICC is reported (the .15 ICC on p.~33 is an a priori power-analysis assumption, NOT an observed design-effect ICC), so icc is left null per spec. TEST-TYPE NUANCE: registry codes the instrument 'Res/Dev'; the ETS literacy assessment was developed independently by ETS under the IES Reading for Understanding grant, was never shared with the program developers/implementers, and is CCSS-aligned -- so it is arguably an independent standardized measure, but I label it researcher_made to match the meta-analysts' coding and the fact that it was custom-built for this research program rather than an off-the-shelf state/commercial test.

effect_sizes.arm_label: iRAISE (Internet-based Reading Apprenticeship) teacher PD vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: ETS scenario-based reading-for-understanding literacy assessment (biology form), developed by Educational Testing Service under the IES Reading for Understanding grant
effect_sizes.timepoint: post / spring 2015 (end of one-year implementation, immediate post-intervention)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's headline covariate/pretest-adjusted effect size = 0.002 (Table 15, p.42): adjusted (regression-benchmark) mean difference = .0005 ETS-scale units standardized by the pooled within-group posttest SD of the recalibrated ETS scale (sqrt(((717-1)*0.242^2+(751-1)*0.249^2)/(717+751-2)) = 0.2456); .0005/0.2456 = 0.00204 ~ 0.002. Hedges' g = J*d with J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1), df = 1466, J = 0.99949, so g = 0.002 (correction negligible). g_se/g_var derived from the report's stated minimum detectable effect size (MDES = 0.19 SD, alpha=.05, 80% power, p.5): SE = 0.19/2.80 = 0.0679, g_var = SE^2 = 0.0046; this design-based SE accounts for the teacher-level clustering. impact_estimate/impact_se fields hold the model-based fixed-effect coefficient for 'Effect of iRAISE for a student with an average pretest' = .003 (SE .004) on the within-grade z-scaled outcome (Table 18, p.45) -- recorded for traceability but NOT used as the g SE because it is on a different (z-transformed) scale than the 0.002 ES; mean_t/mean_c/sd_t/sd_c are the unadjusted descriptive posttest means/SDs from Table 15.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 15 (p.42) headline adjusted ES = 0.002, p=.96, + unadjusted means/SDs/Ns; Table 18 (p.45) model coefficient/SE; Exec. Summary (p.iii) 'no impact of iRAISE on student achievement'; MDES (p.5).
effect_sizes.notes: PRIMARY full-sample confirmatory TPD-vs-control student reading-literacy contrast. iRAISE had NO overall impact on general reading literacy: adjusted ES = 0.002 (p=.96); unadjusted ES = -0.034 (p=.79). Outcome scores are recalibrated/standardized ETS-scale units (control mean 0.013, SD 0.249; iRAISE unadjusted mean 0.009, SD 0.242). Adjusted means both round to 0.013 (true adjusted mean difference = .0005 units). MODERATION (NOT extracted as separate full-sample rows -- these are interaction coefficients, not clean per-subgroup TPD-vs-control mean contrasts, and the report gives no standalone per-subgroup g): (a) impact increased as incoming reading achievement decreased -- interaction coefficient -.006, SE .003, p=.076 (Table 18), i.e. some evidence iRAISE benefited lower-achieving students more; (b) science-pretest interaction -.004, p=.168 (Table 17); (c) by science subject (Table 21): earth/general science impact -.032 (p=.21), with additional impact for biology +.050 (p=.103), chemistry +.013 (p=.682), physics +.054 (p=.103), overall subject-difference p=.17; (d) ELL interaction p=.453 (Table 19, only 13 LEP students); (e) SES interaction -.013, p=.180 favoring higher-SES (Table 20). A sensitivity analysis dropping 6 schools with possibly pre-exposed teachers did not change the result. TEACHER OUTCOMES (NOT student achievement, excluded per spec): significant positive impacts on classroom practice/teacher confidence, ES 0.236-0.619 (e.g. teacher confidence in literacy instruction ES=0.619, p=.004; students practicing comprehension strategies ES=0.516, p=.001; Table 14). For context, the sibling face-to-face RAISE study (Fancsali et al. 2015 = registry row 29) found a +0.32 science-class ES on the same ETS assessment.
